Synopsis:
Dialogue after you destroy the cave-in and set Nere free. Thrinn has been put in charge of getting Nere out, but it's the player who accomplishes it. Nere almost just died from inhaling poisonous gas, so he's very angry. In this dialogue, you determine the fate of the gnomes as well as Nere and the mutinous duergar.

Cluster Contexts:
- UND_TheDrowNere_Mutiny.json: You’re in a tense duergar worksite/checkpoint—hauling rothé, guards, and enslaved gnomes bustle just out of frame—and the player has just blasted open a cave‑in to free the True Soul Nere (Thrinn had been put in charge, but the player accomplished the rescue). Nere nearly suffocated on poisonous gas and is badly shaken, furious, and dangerously unstable; he lashes out at nearby gnomes (examples in the scene include Meerna and Beldron). Off‑screen duergar mutineers and sergeants (names like Brithvar, Morghal, or Thrinn may be present) want to control or punish Nere, and the camp’s hostility means threats of violence are immediate. The player must intervene to stop Nere’s reprisals and decide the fate of the gnomes, Nere, and the mutinous duergar.
- UND_DuergarCamp_LoyalFollowUp.json: Player has sided with Nere, but Nere and Thrinn are dead by the time combat is over. In that case, a duergar initiates dialogue and tells you his plans and you get to decide the gnomes' fate.
- UND_DuergarCamp_RebelGreedyExtort.json: In this dialogue, you have killed Nere without doing the duergar mutineers quest. As a result, they want you to pay for the trouble you've caused. You can give them money, persuade them to let you live, or attack.
- UND_DuergarCamp_RebelsExtort.json: In this dialogue, you have killed Nere without doing the duergar mutineers quest. As a result, they want you to pay for the trouble you've caused. You can give them money, persuade them to let you live, or attack.
- UND_DuergarRebelGreedy_AD_CaveInDestroyed.json: Elder Brithvar comments when cave-in is destroyed. Remarks on how it's time he killed Nere if player took mutiny quest.
